title: Years in which other pay was larger than salary
question: How often is a person’s other pay in a year larger than their regular salary, and is that the year they left?
finding: Since fiscal 2017 there are 1,411 cases of other pay of $25,000 or more that was also larger than the person’s regular salary for the year, $70.2 million in all. In 568 the person does not appear on the payroll again and in 149 only briefly, which is the pattern of a payout on leaving; in 17 the person worked on; 116 are in the latest year and 561 carry names too common to follow. Only 5 of the 1,411 had full-year hours in the year itself. The departments are Fire Department (335), Police (323), Public Health (246) and Public Utilities Commission (98). The largest is $329,750 against a salary of $262,161 (Mark Gonzales, Dep Chf of Dept (Fire Dept) (class 0150), fiscal 2019).
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2017 to 2026: every row where the “other salaries” column is $25,000 or more and exceeds regular salary. Board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out. What happened next is read from later years for the same name, only where the name is rare enough to follow. Largest first. Titles are printed as the payroll prints them (Dep is deputy, Chf is chief, Asst is assistant, Sprv is supervisor, Ofc is officer, EMT is emergency medical technician).
limits: This is mostly what leaving looks like: a person who retires early in a fiscal year earns a few weeks of salary and is paid for years of unused vacation, sick leave and time off in lieu, all of it already earned under the rules of the time. Fire and police lead the list; their labour agreements, which are not on disk, set how much leave may be carried and paid out. A case with full-year hours, or one followed by more years of work, is different in kind and is listed in the next two tables. A name can disappear because the person married, moved to another public employer or died.
